pages.title: Controls
pages.text: The $(l:radiocraft:radios/hf_radios)10m, 20m, 40m and 80m$(/l) radios, the $(l:radiocraft:radios/all_band_radio)all-band$(/l) and the $(l:radiocraft:radios/vhf_base_station)VHF base station$(/l) share one kind of front panel.$(li)$(thing)Knobs$(): scroll, or left click up and right click down. Hover one to read it.$(li)The $(thing)dial$(): scroll, or drag up and down.$(li)Switches and the 80m's mode lever: click a position, or scroll.

pages.title: Knobs
pages.text: $(thing)AF$() is the volume, $(thing)MIC$() your microphone gain and $(thing)SQL$() the squelch.$(br2)The squelch opens on whatever the S-meter reads: the band noise or the strongest station. Once it is open, everything comes through. Turn it just past the noise and the radio stays quiet until a station beats it.

pages.title: AGC
pages.text: The HF panels have an $(thing)AGC$() switch, for how the radio levels what it hears.$(li)$(thing)SLOW$(): the normal sound.$(li)$(thing)FAST$(): the static comes back quickly between words.$(li)$(thing)OFF$(): no levelling. Strong stations blast, weak ones are faint, and the static never ducks.

pages.title: Meter and 10X
pages.text: On receive the meter reads $(thing)S$(), the signal. On the air its selector picks $(thing)PO$(), the power going out, or $(thing)SWR$(). Both read only while power goes out: on SSB only while you talk, on AM and FM whenever you are keyed.$(br2)The $(thing)10X$() key moves the dial ten steps at a time, and UP/DN 100 kHz instead of 10 kHz.

pages.title: QUICK and AM
pages.text: $(thing)Hold QUICK$() to store the frequency you are on. $(thing)Press QUICK$() to jump there, and press it again to come back. The all-band radio changes band to get there.$(br2)Every HF radio has $(thing)AM$() as well as SSB and CW: voice on a steady carrier, as $(l:radiocraft:radios/cb_radios)CB$() uses.

pages.title: Sideband voices
pages.text: An SSB signal is only there while someone talks. The S-meter rises and falls with their words, the squelch opens and shuts with them, and between words the static comes back.$(br2)AM and FM send a steady carrier, so the meter holds still for as long as the far station is keyed.
